sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
**Sources (primary, read this session, no sell-side data):** TXN FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-06, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/97476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm) — segment revenue/profit note, geographic revenue note, cash-flow statement, balance sheet; TXN FY2024 10-K (filed 2025, accession 000009747625000007) for FY2023/FY2024 segment comparatives; TXN Q1 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-04-24, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000101/txn-20260331.htm) — segment margins, inventory, receivables; TI Q4/FY2025 earnings 8-K (2026-01-27, "TI reports Q4 2025 and 2025 financial results") — quarterly depreciation run-rate; TI 2026 Capital Management Review (Feb-2026, investor.ti.com capital-management static files) — capex guidance, FCF/share target, inventory-day target band, fab roadmap (Sherman SM1/SM2, Lehi LFAB1, Richardson RFAB2); TI Q1 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-04-22, CEO Haviv Ilan/CFO Rafael Lizardi); TI Q2 2026 guidance 8-K (2026-07-01 webcast notice) for the imminent 2026-07-22 print.

**EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS gate (run first):**
- Accruals ratio (NI−CFO)/avg total assets: FY2023 = (6,510−6,420)/29,777.5 = **+0.3%**; FY2024 = (4,799−6,318)/33,928.5 = **−4.5%**; FY2025 = (5,001−7,153)/35,047 = **−6.1%**. All well inside the ~10% flag zone and trending MORE negative — CFO increasingly exceeds NI (cash-conversion ratio CFO/NI: 0.99x→1.32x→1.43x, FY23→FY25), a quality positive driven by the rising D&A non-cash add-back, not aggressive accrual.
- Divergence flags: AR grew +14.2% FY25 (1,719→1,963) vs revenue +13.0% — roughly in line, not >1.5x, no flag. Inventory grew +6.1% FY25 (4,527→4,804) vs COGS +16.1% (6,547→7,601 implied) — inventory did NOT outgrow COGS; inventory-days fell 222 (FY25 year-end) → 209 (Q1'26), inside management's stated 150-250-day target band and declining even as shipments recover — supportive of, not contradicting, the margin-inflection thesis. No capitalized-cost creep found. Margin trend and cash conversion are moving together (both improving), not diverging.
- Structure: Ernst & Young LLP, long-tenured auditor; US NASDAQ large-cap 10-K filer; no going-concern/material-weakness language found in the sources reviewed (limited-evidence caveat: full audit-opinion text not directly read this session due to SEC.gov fetch restrictions — relying on secondary synthesis of the filing; flagged, not treated as a pass on faith).
- Related-party gravity: none material identified — checked, none found.
- Action rule: no confirmed manipulation-class flag → gate clears, proceed to estimates.

**Revenue build (segment, USD million):** FY2023 Analog 13,040 / Embedded 3,370 / Total 17,519. FY2024 Analog 12,160 (−6.8%) / Embedded 2,530 (−24.9%) / Other ~951 / Total 15,641 — the trough year, both segments correcting hard off elevated 2021-22 channel inventory. FY2025 Analog 14,006 (+15.2%) / Embedded 2,697 (+6.6%) / Other 979 / Total 17,682 (+13.0%), with segment operating margin 38.6% (Analog) / 11.3% (Embedded). Q1 2026: Analog $3.92bn (+22% YoY, op margin 41.7%), Embedded $723m (+12% YoY, op margin 16.9% vs 6.2% a year ago) — a large, filing-confirmed margin inflection already underway, not a forecast. My forward build (segment growth decelerating off the Q1 snap-back rate, not extrapolating it): Analog +14%/+9%/+8%/+7% and Embedded +10%/+8%/+7%/+6% for FY26-29E, Other flat ~+3%/yr → Total revenue 19,942 (FY26E, +12.8%) / 21,646 (FY27E, +8.5%) / 23,293 (FY28E, +7.6%) / 24,847 (FY29E, +6.7%).

**Capex/depreciation cycle (the core mechanism) and margin path:** Capex peaked at $5,071m in FY2023, then $4,820m (FY24), $4,550m (FY25); TI's Feb-2026 Capital Management Day guided FY26 capex to **$2.0-3.0bn** (management: "toward the lower end if growth is similar to last year"), with a stated long-run framework of **10-15% of revenue for FY27+** — a genuine, disclosed step-down, not my assumption. Depreciation is the lagging offset: $1,175m (FY23) → $1,508m (FY24) → an estimated ~$1.85-1.95bn (FY25, derived from Q4'25 run-rate of $537m vs Q4'24's $416m, since the FY25 full-year figure was not directly extracted from the primary source this session) → guided $2.2-2.4bn (FY26) — i.e., D&A is STILL rising into 2026 even as capex falls, meaning the gross-margin drag has not fully cleared. I model consolidated operating margin 34.1% (FY25A) → 36.5% (FY26E) → 38.5% (FY27E) → 40.0% (FY28E) → 41.0% (FY29E), a deliberate fade well short of the FY2021-22 peak (~49-51%) since the depreciation base is now structurally ~2x larger and I do not assume full reversion.

**Owner-earnings bridge / reinvestment rate / ROIIC (VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY contract):** FY25 NOPAT ≈ operating profit $6,023m × (1−12.5% effective tax rate, per company disclosure of a ~12-13% rate) ≈ $5,270m. Invested capital (equity $16,273m + total debt $14,048m − cash&STI $4,881m) = $25,440m (FY25) vs $22,919m (FY24, equity $16,903m + debt $13,596m − cash&STI $7,580m) → avg $24,180m → **ROIC ≈ 21.8%**, consistent with third-party ROIC reads (~20-23% TTM) as a cross-check. FY25 net reinvestment = (capex $4,550m − D&A ~$1,900m) + partial ΔNWC proxy (Δinventory $277m + ΔAR $244m, AP not captured this session) ≈ $3,171m → **reinvestment rate ≈ 60% of NOPAT** (high, reflecting the still-live buildout). Owner earnings FY25 = CFO $7,153m − a maintenance-capex proxy (using management's own 10-15%-of-revenue long-run framework, midpoint 12.5% × $17,682m ≈ $2,210m) − SBC $419m (subtracted per house method as a real economic/dilution cost, not a non-cash wash) ≈ **$4,524m** (~$4.94/share on 914m diluted shares) — a stricter, lower figure than management's own reported FCF/share of $3.23 (FY25) precisely because management's FCF does not subtract SBC. Forward: my FY26-29E build implies owner earnings/share rising from ~$5.8 (FY26E) to ~$7.8 (FY29E) — directionally consistent with, but below, management's own >$8/share FY26 FCF target (their metric excludes the SBC haircut and likely assumes faster top-line conversion than my deliberately conservative segment build).

**3-assumption sensitivity:** (1) FY26 Analog growth: base +14% vs Q1's +22% YoY print (assumes deceleration as the snap-back laps); bull ~+20% if it holds; bear +8% if China/higher-for-longer bites. (2) Operating margin path: base 34%→41% (FY25→FY29); bear plateaus ~37-38% if depreciation growth doesn't decelerate as guided; bull reaches mid-40s if opex leverage beats plan. (3) Fade/discount: base COE 9%, terminal g 2.5% (= 8.7% steady-state reinvestment rate × ~25% steady-state ROIIC), moat-supported slow fade to COE by ~year 15; bear uses the card's year-10 default cliff with no moat credit (lower fair multiple, reinforcing caution below); bull assumes near-perpetual ROIIC ~25% (close to what current price appears to require) — this bull case is plausible but is not my base case.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.detail: one sentence, from memory, written before document work
sections.markdown: What I believe the market narrative is: The market narrative on TXN is "quality analog/embedded semis compounder, long capital-return history, but stuck in a multi-year capex-driven margin trough from its 300mm fab buildout while auto/industrial end-markets stay weak, and now getting a secondary bid as a 'safe' domestic-manufacturing/onshoring and rate-cut-beneficiary trade rather than a direct AI story."

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** The multi-year capex-driven margin/FCF trough (2023-2025) is over; the Feb-2026 Capital Management Day guidance (capex cut to $2-3bn, FCF/share target >$8) confirms an inflection, and TI deserves a re-rated multiple as a widening-moat 300mm-cost-position compounder — a view the market has already substantially acted on (+32%/12m, +67%/6m, screen row market-data snapshot).

**Why wrong:** We do not dispute the mechanism — it is real, filing-confirmed (Embedded op margin 6.2%→16.9% YoY in Q1'26 alone), and our own bottom-up build (constructed before viewing price) supports the DIRECTION of the consensus story. Where we differ is magnitude/price, not direction — that is a thin edge and we say so plainly. Running our own reinvestment-rate × ROIIC framework at a disciplined 9% COE and 2.5% terminal g (moat-adjusted slow fade to year ~15), fair EV/EBIT works out to **~12-14x**. At last price $311.46, EV (mkt cap $284.7bn + net debt $9.2bn = $293.9bn) is **~40x** our FY26E operating profit ($7,279m) and still **~29x** our FY29E operating profit ($10,187m) — a genuine, filings-derived gap, not a "feels expensive" comment, and one that persists even under our reasonably bullish forward margin path. The market may be paying for a longer/stronger fade than we think prudent, and appears to be underweighting that ~50% of TXN revenue ships into China (10-K geographic note) against the current "China weak/un-reflating" macro read (the macro regime memo, 2026-07-11) — a direct risk to the volume-recovery leg the entire operating-leverage mechanism depends on.

**What proves us wrong:** If Q2 2026 (2026-07-22) and following quarters show Analog/Embedded margins continuing to expand sequentially, China-linked industrial/auto demand holds up despite the weak-China macro read, and the multiple holds or extends further without any reversion toward our ~12-14x EBIT anchor — i.e., the market successfully underwrites a longer, stronger fade than our base case — we are wrong and this compounds as a genuine long from here.

**Edge taxonomy:** Primarily **(a) analytical** — the reinvestment-rate × ROIIC / multiple-survival test disciplines the price paid rather than just endorsing the direction of the story. Secondary **(b) informational-synthesis** — combining Capital Management Day capex/FCF guidance, Q1'26 segment margin prints, the China ship-to exposure, and the current macro regime into one risk-adjusted read. Explicitly NOT (c) time-arbitrage or (d) structural-flow. We are honest that this is not a strong variant view on direction — after the documents, our fundamental read matches an informed generalist's; the only real edge is discipline on entry price and an explicit China-risk flag the price action does not appear to reflect. TXN sits in the MOMENTUM sleeve and we are not endorsing the momentum — our own valuation work argues for caution at the current print, which is why entry is set below market and ev_math is shaded to a small negative expected value at last price.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: >=3, observable, current, each citing a dossier/filing line
sections.markdown:
1. ~50% of TXN revenue ships into China by destination (FY2025 10-K geographic-revenue note, ~20% by customer HQ) even as the current macro regime read is "China weak/un-reflating" (the macro regime memo, 2026-07-11) — a direct threat to the volume leg the margin-inflection mechanism depends on.
2. Depreciation is STILL rising into 2026 (guided $2.2-2.4bn vs an estimated ~$1.9bn FY2025, itself up from $1.175bn FY2023 per the FY2023/FY2024 10-K cash-flow statements) even as capex falls — the gross-margin drag from the fab buildout has not fully cleared, and the market's rapid re-rating may be front-running a cleaner inflection than the P&L has delivered yet.
3. At last price $311.46, TXN trades at ~29-40x our own forward operating-profit estimates versus a ~12-14x "fair" EV/EBIT implied by our reinvestment-rate × ROIIC framework at a 9% COE — a filings-derived valuation gap (Bottom-up estimates section above), not a subjective view.
4. Embedded Processing revenue fell 25% from FY2023 ($3.37bn) to FY2024 ($2.53bn) before recovering (FY2025 10-K segment note) — the capacity now inflecting margins has real order-cycle volatility; one strong quarter (Q1'26 +12% YoY) does not retire that risk.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is mid-2029 (long horizon, per derated_compounder_rerating's 3y window) and this position lost roughly 30%. The most likely reason is that we were largely RIGHT on the fundamental mechanism — capex did fall, depreciation growth did decelerate, Analog/Embedded margins did keep expanding through 2026-27 much as modeled — but we were WRONG on the price paid: the entry multiple (~40x forward EBIT even after a 5% discipline discount to last price) never had room to expand further and instead mean-reverted a meaningful way toward the ~12-14x "fair" anchor our own framework implied, so multiple compression outran EBIT growth. A secondary, compounding path: China-linked industrial/auto end-demand (≈50% ship-to exposure) rolled over harder than the Q1'26 snap-back implied under the "China weak/un-reflating" regime, stalling the volume recovery the whole operating-leverage story needs, which shows up first as inventory days breaking back above the 250-day ceiling (our kpi kill criterion) before it shows up in the multiple.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
(Drew appends verbatim; survives the Judge verdict — never edited by a later stage)

**BEAR — Drew — 2026-07-11T14:42:35Z — VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED**

**0. Fact-check (I verified the three load-bearing numbers against primary sources myself — all clean, which HELPS the kill, not the trade):**
- Q1'26 segment margins: Analog $3.92bn +22% YoY at 41.7% op margin; Embedded $723m +12% YoY, op margin 16.9% (from 6.2%) — VERIFIED (TXN Q1'26 10-Q, txn-20260331; corroborated by the 2026-04-22 call). Accurate.
- Feb-2026 Capital Management: FY26 capex $2-3bn ("toward the lower end if growth similar"), long-run 10-15% of revenue, ">$8/share FCF on track" — VERIFIED (TI Feb-2026 Capital Management materials; press 2026-02-28). Accurate.
- China ship-to ~50% / end-customer HQ ~20% (FY25) — VERIFIED verbatim in the FY2025 10-K geographic note. Accurate.
- FY25: total $17.68bn (+13.0%), Analog $14,006m (+15%, 38.6% op margin), Embedded $2.70bn — VERIFIED. Accurate.
There is no factual escape hatch here. The analyst got the facts right and the trade is STILL a negative-EV long. That is the cleanest possible kill: I cannot rescue this by correcting an error, because there is no error — the honest facts produce a losing bet.

**1. Estimates at bear value — the EV is WORSE than the -3.14% shown, not understated-in-your-favor.** The ev_math is anchored to a wished-for entry of $296, ~5% below the last print of $311.46 (max_chase 3% → best realistic fill ~$305; the $296 fill may never trigger). Re-run at last price: down-to-kill (207.2) = -33.5%, up-to-target (390.72) = +25.4% → price EV = 0.35(25.4) − 0.65(33.5) = **−12.9%**, ~−7.7% after 3y of dividends. The one flattering assumption in the whole model is a fill that may not happen; remove it and EV roughly doubles the loss. My widest-honest-error-bar parameterization (p_up 0.25, up +25, p_down 0.75, down −50) yields **≈ −27%** — see §5 for why −30% understates true downside.

**2. Variant perception — this is not a thin edge, it is a NULL edge, and the analyst says so in writing.** The thesis states: *"our fundamental read matches an informed generalist's; the only real edge is discipline on entry price."* That is an admission of no edge. "Discipline on price paid" is not an edge — a limit order 5% under the last print is available to every participant on earth. Worse: the thesis's OWN valuation section pegs fair EV/EBIT at **12-14x**, i.e. fair value ≈ **$85-102/share** (12-14× FY26E op profit $7,279m, less $9.2bn net debt, ÷914m shares). Buying at $296 is therefore paying **~3x the analyst's own fair value** and calling the 5% haircut "discipline." Anchoring to the wrong number by 5% is not discipline. The claimed edge does not exist.

**3. Internal contradiction — THE single strongest point, and it means the EV OVERSTATES the trade's appeal.** The valuation/disconfirming section says fair EV/EBIT is 12-14x (→ ~67-73% downside from spot). The exit_plan target is **$390.72 (+25% above spot)**, which is ~34x FY29E and ~50x FY26E op profit — **2.5-3.5x the analyst's own fair multiple.** You cannot simultaneously hold that 12-14x is fair AND set a target that requires the market to keep paying 34-50x. The "+32% up case" that props up p_up×up_pct is manufactured by assuming the very multiple your own framework calls unwarranted not only persists but that the stock climbs from here. That is *"multiple expansion wearing a DCF costume"* — the exact defect VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY §4 says to flag. Strip it out and anchor the up-case to the analyst's own fair value: up_pct is negative and honest EV is **≈ −40%**, not −3.14%. The two-point schema does not understate a hidden asymmetry — it *flatters* the trade. There is no buried optionality; the truth is uglier than the number.

**4. Wrong base rate — reclassify and it auto-kills.** `derated_compounder_rerating` requires a name that *"suffered multiple compression, re-rating as growth resumes"* and, per the base-rate library, *"only a cyclical or sentiment de-rating with intact competitive position clears this archetype... the trap is a STRUCTURAL de-rating (local-challenger share loss) masquerading as a cyclical one."* TXN has ALREADY re-rated (+32%/12m, +67%/6m, −6.3% off 52w high) and sits in the **MOMENTUM** sleeve. The compression is spent; the analyst is buying the re-rated name at ~40x forward EBIT, the opposite of buying a derated compounder. On the momentum reading, base_rates is explicit: *"a momentum-only thesis with no variant perception is an auto-kill"* — and per §2 the analyst has conceded no variant perception. And the competitive position is NOT intact (§6). The archetype is misapplied; under the correct one, house law kills it on sight.

**5. Sizing — dead on arrival by the fund's own discipline.** kill 207.2 < entry 296 < target 390.72 orders correctly; |down|=30.0% and up=32.0% both sit inside the ±3pp band **off the $296 entry** — internally consistent, but consistent about a losing bet. Expected_pct is NEGATIVE (−3.14% at entry, ~−7.7% at last price, ≈−27% to −40% at honest bear/own-fair-value inputs). Quarter-Kelly of a negative edge is a **negative/zero position** — the sizing engine cannot return a positive script_pct on expected_pct<0 without violating SIZING_EV_BASE_RATES. And the −30% down_pct is itself charitable: the analyst's own 12-14x fair value implies a full multiple reversion of **−65% to −73%**, so a kill "stop" at −30% assumes an orderly exit that a multiple gap will not grant. No position size clears the bar. The trade is dead on arrival.

**6. NEW disconfirming facts (not in the thesis) — the China risk is STRUCTURAL, not the cyclical-volume risk the thesis frames.**
- (a) **China anti-dumping probe targeting TI specifically + accelerating localization.** In Sept-2025 China's MOFCOM opened an anti-dumping investigation into imported US analog chips naming **Texas Instruments, Broadcom, Onsemi, ADI** (citing US analog imports +37% 2022-24 while prices fell 52%). China analog localization rose 9% (2019) → 16% (2024) and is accelerating; domestic challengers SG Micro, 3Peak, Novosense grew revenue/profit ~35-100% CAGR and are taking share. TI's THIRD price hike in 12 months (announced May-2026, effective 2026-07-01) is *itself* accelerating substitution. This converts ~50% of ship-to revenue from "China cyclically weak" into "China structurally de-Americanizing its analog supply chain and investigating TI for dumping" — precisely the *"local-challenger share loss masquerading as cyclical"* trap that disqualifies the archetype. (Sources: Reuters/TrendForce coverage of the MOFCOM probe; 36Kr/CSIS on localization.) The bull case is self-undermining: the 41.7% margin is powered by price hikes that trigger the very substitution and duties that kill the volume leg.
- (b) **The capital-return "moat" is running on the balance sheet.** FY25 cash returned = **$6.476bn** ($4.999bn dividends + $1.477bn buybacks) on trailing FCF of only **~$2.94bn** — a **320% payout**; dividends alone were ~1.7x FCF. Cash fell $7.58bn → $4.88bn and debt sits at ~$14bn. If the margin inflection stalls, TI either breaks its dividend-growth streak (violent de-rating of the "safe compounder / rate-cut-beneficiary" bid the screen is buying) or levers up further into a higher-for-longer regime (screen factor2 = us_rates). Neither is in the thesis. (Source: TI Q4/FY2025 8-K.)

**7. Steelman pre-mortem — three unmentioned failure modes.** The pre-mortem covers only "right-on-mechanism-wrong-on-price" and "China cyclical volume rollover." It omits: (c) **structural China share loss / anti-dumping duties** permanently impairing ~50% ship-to revenue (§6a); (d) **dividend/return unsustainability** forcing either a payout cut or higher leverage (§6b); (e) **the negative feedback between margin and volume** — margins are propped by price hikes that accelerate the substitution/duty risk, so the bull and bear legs are not independent as the model assumes. Any of the three breaks the thesis before the "wrong-on-price" slow-bleed even plays out.

**8. Anti-gaming inspection.** Timestamps are clean: estimates committed 14:36:51Z before the 14:40:00Z draft (estimates-first holds), and p_up was shaded DOWN to 0.35 from the 0.40 base rate — honest, not gamed up. BUT: (i) the number that IS inflated is up_pct/target — the $390.72 target contradicts the analyst's own 12-14x fair value (§3), which is where an even-more-negative EV is being avoided; (ii) the EARNINGS_QUALITY gate is admittedly NOT fully verified — the analyst did not read the audit opinion ("SEC.gov fetch restrictions... secondary synthesis... not a pass on faith"); under fail-closed, an unread quality gate is not a pass; (iii) FY25 depreciation — a load-bearing input to the entire capex/D&A margin mechanism — is admittedly "estimated ~$1.85-1.95bn, not directly extracted from the primary source"; the core mechanism rests partly on a guessed number; (iv) horizon="long" with catalyst_date=null, yet the binding trigger is Q2 earnings on **2026-07-22 — 11 days out**: a negative-EV long being initiated days before a binary print, either mislabeled (should carry a declared event) or, if genuinely long-horizon, with no reason to enter now rather than after the print.

**9. VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED.** *A long whose own author concedes zero directional edge, whose own fair-value math (12-14x EBIT ≈ $85-102) sits ~70% below the price being paid, and whose largest revenue geography (~50% ship-to China) faces an active anti-dumping probe and accelerating domestic substitution, is not a "disciplined compounder" — it is a negative-EV momentum chase mislabeled as a value entry, and it should never reach a PM.*

**BEAR RE-ATTACK — Drew — 2026-07-12T04:15:10Z — VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED**

**1. Coverage — every numbered point answered, none dodged.** I checked the Revision against all nine of my original points one by one. §0 correctly notes there was never a factual error to fix. §1 concedes the fill-risk point and correctly declines to move `entry_plan.level` (that field is Phase-2 analyst-drafted, but per the schema up_pct/down_pct are defined off entry, not spot — moving entry lower would mechanically improve *both* legs of ev_math since kill/target are fixed dollar levels further from a cheaper entry; leaving it at 296 is the non-flattering choice, correctly made). §2 concedes "no edge" in full, without qualification. §3 is the strongest section — it doesn't just accept my number, it independently re-derives a second, harder version of the same point (entry-side EV/FY29E-op-profit multiple) that I hadn't run. §4 concedes archetype misfit and correctly declines to change `archetype:` itself (genuinely not theirs to rule on) while flagging the reclassification question to the Judge. §5 acknowledges its own recomputed EV is worse than my bear-case parameterization, not better — the correct comparison. §6 absorbs both new disconfirming facts without trying to spin either. §7 concedes the pre-mortem gaps without pretending to backfill them outside scope. §8 re-affirms both open anti-gaming caveats (unread audit opinion, estimated FY25 D&A) rather than quietly closing them. Nothing here is a diplomatic hedge dressed as a concession.

**2. Arithmetic re-derived independently — every material number checks out exactly, no sign errors, no cherry-picking in the mechanics.**
- Kill level: 12x and 14x × FY26E op profit $7,279m (= FY26E revenue $19,942m × 36.5% margin, both from the untouched committed Bottom-up section) = $87,348m/$101,906m, less $9.2bn net debt, ÷914m diluted shares = **$85.5–$101.4/share**; midpoint ≈ $93.5 → **matches the frontmatter $93.50 exactly.**
- down_pct: (93.50−296)/296 = **−68.41%**, matches the stated −68.4% to a rounding hair.
- Entry-side EV/FY29E multiple: mkt cap at $296 (296×914m=$270.5bn) + $9.2bn net debt = **$279.7bn**; FY29E op profit = FY29E revenue $24,847m × 41.0% margin = $10,187m; $279.7bn/$10,187m = **27.5x**, matches the claimed figure and is itself derived from the frozen Bottom-up numbers, not invented.
- expected_pct: 0.15×32 + 0.85×(−68.4) + 1.82×3 − 0.3 = 4.8 − 58.14 + 5.46 − 0.3 = **−48.18%**, matches exactly, using the identical formula structure as the pre-revision −3.14% (verified that one too: 0.35×32+0.65×(−30)+1.82×3−0.3=−3.14). Same method, honestly re-applied to worse inputs — not a reverse-engineered number dressed up to look derived.
No hidden lever was pulled to manufacture the more negative number; base_rate.rate=p_up=0.15 is the disclosed shaded prior with "no further optimistic deviation argued," not an arbitrary dial-turn.

**3. New anti-gaming inspection — one real but minor residual tilt, one non-numeric scope overreach, one systemic (not new) gap.**
(a) **Residual favorable framing, doesn't change the verdict:** §3's entry-multiple point uses FY29E op profit (the most generous, furthest-out denominator) to get 27.5x, when the more standard near-term framing (FY26E op profit $7,279m) gives **~38.4x** — a full ~3x the fair anchor, not ~2x. Both numbers indict the entry; FY29E is simply the gentler of the two available. Worth naming, not worth weighting — the conclusion survives either way.
(b) **Scope claim doesn't hold up on re-read, but it's a paperwork miss, not a numeric one.** The Revision repeatedly declines to set `catalyst_date` (2026-07-22 is 10 days out, per my original §8iv), citing fields it "has authority to edit" as limited to kill_criteria/ev_math/base_rate. I re-read fund record's actual Revision protocol: the only explicit freeze is on "committed estimates" (the Bottom-up section, per Phase-1 step 4) plus the new-evidence gate on raising p_up/up_pct/target. Nothing there restricts `catalyst_date`. Passing a one-line, purely-honest, zero-controversy fix to "the Judge/orchestrator" when the analyst could have just made it is mild performative deference — it costs nothing numerically and doesn't rescue the trade, but it's an invented scope limit, not a real one.
(c) **Checked for a missing stage_log stamp, found it — but it's house-wide, not specific to this revision.** No `{stage: revised, ...}` entry was appended despite the Revision existing in the body. I checked the other thesis files carrying a "## Revision" section (T-GLOBAL-SMFG-001, T-INDO-ELSA-001 via reference, T-INDO-PNBN-001) — none of them append a revision stage_log stamp either, and `the thesis linter`'s stage_log check only enforces attacked-before-judged ordering and monotonic timestamps, not a revision stamp. This is a norm without a ruler (fund record meta-principle 1) across the whole pipeline, not something gamed in this file specifically. Flagging for QC awareness, not holding it against this analyst.

**4. Net effect: if anything, the Revision still UNDERSTATES the damage, on four specific points.**
- The dividend credit is stale against the Revision's own new evidence. `net_div_yield_pct_pa` stays at 1.82%/yr — unchanged — even though §6b (a fact this Revision itself introduces) argues the FY25 payout ran ~320% of FCF and is plausibly unsustainable under margin stress. The kill scenario IS the margin-stress scenario. Crediting three full years of an at-risk dividend inside the loss leg of expected_pct is generous to the trade; a dividend cut concurrent with the kill firing would make the true down-case worse than −68.4%+div, not equal to it.
- Treating archetype fit as merely "a live, unresolved structural question for the Judge" undersells how closed this already is: §2 concedes zero edge unconditionally (not contingent on which archetype applies), and `momentum_continuation`'s own registry notes say a momentum-only thesis with no variant perception is an auto-kill. Under the current label the structural-de-rating trap applies; under the alternative label the no-edge auto-kill applies. Either way it's dead before expected_pct is even computed — the −48.18% is confirmatory, not load-bearing.
- No allowance anywhere in the math for ARB/gap risk on a stock that gets a binary print 10 days after entry — my own method card's own duty (attack protocol §5) is that a fired kill can clear 1-2 bands below the kill level on a gap. None of that tail is in −68.4%; a bad Q2 print could realize a worse fill than the modeled kill level.
- The kill trigger sits at the midpoint of the analyst's own $85-102 fair-value band rather than the top ($101 ≈ −65.9%), which would fire earlier and cap the loss sooner — marginally softer than the Revision's own stated principle that "a kill should fire ahead of the worst case." Small, non-decisive, but it is a residual softness, not a residual harshness.

**5. VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED — confirmed, not softened.** The Revision is honest work, not a survival attempt dressed as one: it re-derives my own numbers independently rather than parroting them, concedes the null edge without qualification, and lands on an expected_pct (−48.18%) that is worse than my own harshest parameterization (−27% to −40%) using nothing but its own house method and its own already-committed estimates. The single strongest sentence: *the Revision's own recomputed −48.18% is best read as a floor, not a bottom — it still credits three years of a dividend its own new evidence says may not survive the very margin-stress scenario the kill price is built on, and it treats a double auto-kill (structural-derating trap or momentum-no-edge, under either archetype label) as an open question rather than a foregone one.*

**ANALYST_GLOBAL (Sloane) — Revision — 2026-07-12T03:36:38Z — responding to Drew's 2026-07-11T14:42:35Z KILL_RECOMMENDED**

Net effect of this revision: p_up and base_rate.rate cut by more than half, the kill price reset to the analyst's own fair-value anchor (down_pct widened from -30% to -68.4%), and the archetype's fitness for this name conceded as doubtful. Nothing is raised: entry, target, and up_pct are left exactly as drafted (house convention — see #3/#8i below for why I address the target problem through probability rather than by moving it). Recomputed expected_pct is **-48.18%**, not -3.14%. I do not believe this trade survives.

**0. Fact-check — conceded with no numeric change required.** Drew re-verified the four load-bearing facts (Q1'26 segment margins, Feb-2026 Capital Management guidance, ~50% China ship-to, FY25 segment results) independently against primary sources and found them accurate. This is the cleanest possible form of a kill: there is no factual error to correct, which means nothing below is a "fix" — it is a re-weighting of honest numbers I already had, plus new facts (§6) I did not have.

**1. EV worse at the real fill price.** Drew's arithmetic is correct as a what-if: at last price ($311.46) or the more realistic ~$305 fill implied by a 3% max-chase against that print, down-to-kill and up-to-target both worsen versus the $296 entry basis. House convention anchors ev_math to the committed entry_plan.level, not to spot, and I am not moving entry_plan.level=296 here — that is PM/execution territory. But per the Revision protocol's instruction to say so explicitly rather than silently changing it: Drew is right that the $296 limit, sitting ~5% below a print that just ran hard, may not fill at all. I flag this to Harrison (PM_GLOBAL) explicitly. It is a second-order point next to §3 below, however — even a successful fill at the disciplined $296 entry is a bad trade once the up-case is probability-weighted honestly (see recomputed expected_pct).

**2. Variant perception is a null edge, not a thin one — conceded in full.** My own words — "our fundamental read matches an informed generalist's; the only real edge is discipline on entry price" — are an admission of no edge, and Drew is right to call it one. A 5% limit under the last print is available to any participant with a keyboard; it is not an edge, and I should not have framed it as one. I withdraw the edge claim as stated. What's left is (b) informational-synthesis on the China risk (§6 makes this worse, not better, for the long) — which cuts against the position, not for it.

**3. Internal contradiction on the target multiple — the single point that does the most damage, and I've re-derived it independently rather than just accepting Drew's number.** Drew is right that fair EV/EBIT (12-14x, from my own Variant perception DCF at 9% COE / 2.5% terminal g) implies fair value of roughly $85-102/share (12-14x FY26E op profit $7,279m, less $9.2bn net debt, over 914m shares) — call it ~$93.5 at the midpoint. I checked the entry side too: EV at the $296 entry is ~$279.8bn (mkt cap $270.6bn + net debt $9.2bn), which is **~27.5x my own FY29E operating-profit estimate** ($10,187m) — already roughly 2x my own fair anchor before the target is even considered. Any price above $296 mechanically requires that FY29E-basis multiple to be higher still, not lower — the entry itself, not just the $390.72 target, is already underwriting a persistently rich multiple relative to my own DCF. That is the real defect: my exit_plan rationale claimed "no further re-rating leg... is underwritten," but I never checked that claim against my own fair-multiple output, and it does not hold up — the $390.72 target implies ~34-36x FY29E / ~50x FY26E operating profit, 2.5-3.5x my own fair anchor, exactly as Drew computed. I am **not** lowering entry (§1) or target/up_pct here, for a structural reason: any target low enough to be genuinely consistent with a 12-14x fair multiple sits *below* $296 (I checked — even a generous 20x FY29E multiple implies ~$213/share, and the schema requires target > entry for a long). There is no honest target above entry that this framework can produce. Rather than manufacture an arbitrary "just above entry" number that would look disciplined but isn't actually derived from anything, I am leaving target/up_pct untouched and doing the only thing left within my authority that is both honest and structurally valid: crushing the probability I assign to reaching it (§4) and resetting the downside to where my own framework says fair value actually sits (kill 207.2 → 93.50; frontmatter). That combination is how this revision expresses "Drew is right" without gaming the schema.

**4. Wrong base rate / archetype fit — largely conceded.** `derated_compounder_rerating`'s own notes require "only a cyclical or sentiment de-rating with intact competitive position" and warn explicitly against "a STRUCTURAL de-rating (local-challenger share loss) masquerading as a cyclical one." TXN has already re-rated (+32%/12m) and sits in the MOMENTUM sleeve — not a fresh de-rated entry — and §6a's new evidence (active MOFCOM anti-dumping probe naming TXN + accelerating Chinese analog localization) is precisely the local-challenger-share-loss trap the archetype warns about. I do not have authority under this Revision protocol to change the `archetype:` frontmatter key itself (only kill_criteria/ev_math/base_rate are mine to touch here) — I flag explicitly for the Judge that reclassification toward `momentum_continuation` (rate 0.50, but whose own registry note reads "a momentum-only thesis with no variant perception is an auto-kill" — which, per §2's conceded null edge, this now is) is a live, unresolved structural question this revision does not settle. Within the current archetype label, I am cutting base_rate.rate and ev_math.p_up from 0.40/0.35 to **0.15** (frontmatter) — the shaded prior itself, with no further optimistic deviation argued, per SIZING_EV_BASE_RATES §2 ("if you can't name the reference class, p is fiction").

**5. Sizing — dead on arrival, and worse under my own revised numbers.** Recomputed expected_pct is -48.18% (0.15×32 + 0.85×(-68.4) + 1.82×3 - 0.3), materially worse than Drew's own -27% to -40% "honest error bar" estimates, not better. Quarter-Kelly (or any Kelly) of an expected_pct this negative is a negative/zero position; the sizing engine cannot and should not return a positive script_pct here. On the kill-level charitable point specifically: I have reset the kill price from the arbitrary 207.2 to $93.50 — the midpoint of my own fair-EV/EBIT-implied value — which is a materially more honest "where this actually re-rates to if the mechanism fails" level than a technical stop was. I have not adopted Drew's full -73% low end as the kill trigger itself (a kill should fire on the way down, ahead of the worst case completing, not equal the worst case) — but I flag the tail beyond -68.4% explicitly for PM/Risk Officer gap-risk sizing, especially given TXN's own elevated multiple and the binary Q2 print 11 days out.

**6. New disconfirming facts — accepted in full; both cut against the long, so nothing here can be used to raise anything.** (a) The Sept-2025 MOFCOM anti-dumping probe naming TXN specifically, plus accelerating China analog localization (9%→16%, 2019-2024) and fast-growing domestic challengers (SG Micro/3Peak/Novosense), converts what my thesis framed as cyclical China softness into a plausible structural share-loss story — and TXN's own May-2026 price hike (third in 12 months) plausibly accelerates the substitution it is trying to outrun. I had not seen this; it is dated, sourced, and load-bearing, and it is the primary reason base_rate.rate/p_up are cut as hard as they are in §4, not merely trimmed. (b) The 320% FY25 cash-return payout (dividends 1.7x FCF alone) against a shrinking cash balance is a real, unmodeled tail risk to the "safe compounder" framing the stock's re-rating leans on — a margin stall forces a choice between a dividend cut (a violent de-rating of exactly the multiple this thesis is long) or further leverage into a higher-for-longer regime. Both facts belong in the "Disconfirming facts" list at the next redraft cycle; that section is outside this Revision's edit scope, so I flag it here for the record rather than editing it.

**7. Steelman pre-mortem gaps — conceded, not separately re-modeled.** The original pre-mortem covered "right on mechanism, wrong on price" and cyclical China volume rollover; it did not cover (c) structural China share loss/anti-dumping duties, (d) dividend/payout unsustainability, or (e) the negative feedback between price hikes (which prop up the 41.7% Analog margin) and the substitution/duty risk those same hikes accelerate. I cannot edit the Pre-mortem section under this Revision's scope (frontmatter + this section only) — flagging for the record that (c)/(d)/(e) are real, unpriced failure modes, and noting that (e) in particular means the bull and bear legs of this trade are not independent, which the two-point ev_math schema cannot express directly but the crushed p_up in §4 partially absorbs.

**8. Anti-gaming inspection.** (i) Drew is right that up_pct/target were the inflated element (§3) — addressed there by leaving them untouched and instead pricing them at a much lower probability, rather than by quietly moving the goalposts. (ii) The EARNINGS_QUALITY gate's audit-opinion sub-check remains unread this session (SEC.gov fetch restriction noted in the original gate write-up) — under fail-closed this stays an open, unresolved caveat; I have no new document access in this Revision pass to close it, so I flag it plainly rather than paper over it. (iii) The FY25 depreciation figure (~$1.85-1.95bn) feeding the core capex/D&A margin mechanism remains an estimate, not a directly-extracted primary-source number — an inherited limitation of the committed Bottom-up section, which I cannot edit under protocol; flagged, not fixed. (iv) horizon="long" with catalyst_date=null sitting against a binding Q2 print 11 days out (2026-07-22) is a fair mislabeling flag — I recommend the Judge/orchestrator set catalyst_date to 2026-07-22, but catalyst_date is not among the fields (kill_criteria price, ev_math, base_rate) I have authority to edit in this Revision pass, so I am not setting it myself.

**9. Verdict — I do not contest it.** Drew's cleanest sentence — got the facts right and the trade is still negative-EV — holds up after independent re-derivation, not just acceptance: the entry itself prices at ~27.5x my own FY29E operating-profit estimate against a self-computed fair anchor of 12-14x, before the target's further multiple-expansion problem is even considered (§3), and a new, dated, sourced fact (§6a) plausibly converts the largest single revenue-geography risk from cyclical to structural. Recomputed expected_pct is **-48.18%** on my own house method, using my own already-written fair-value work, not Drew's harshest parameterization. I am not recommending this be saved.

**Frontmatter changes made this revision (within Revision-protocol authority only: kill_criteria price, ev_math, base_rate):**
- `kill_criteria[0].value`: 207.2 → 93.50 (down_pct -30% → -68.4%; reasons §3/§5 above).
- `base_rate`: rate 0.40 → 0.15; source updated to cite the archetype-fitness concession (§4/§6a).
- `ev_math`: p_up 0.35 → 0.15, p_down 0.65 → 0.85, down_pct -30 → -68.4, expected_pct -3.14 → -48.18. up_pct (32), net_div_yield_pct_pa (1.82), fee_tax_drag_pct (0.3) unchanged.
- entry_plan, exit_plan.target, Bottom-up estimates section, estimates_committed_at, stage_log, status, and verdict: untouched, per protocol.

**Routing note (procedural, not mine to decide).** Per the fund record Revision protocol, several ev_math fields moved far more than 20% relative to their pre-attack values: p_up (-57% relative), down_pct (+128% relative wider), base_rate.rate (-62.5% relative), and expected_pct (a sign-preserving but ~15x relative move, -3.14 → -48.18). That sends this thesis back to Drew for a fact-check pass before the Judge, per the stated routing rule. Every change here moves further against the trade, so I would expect that pass to confirm KILL_RECOMMENDED rather than reopen the case, but the protocol step should not be skipped.
